title: Gang Violence Continues Nan Brooklyn for Second Day — Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, Delmas 2 and 4 Seized
detail: On May 27, 2026 — the second consecutive day of gang offensives in and around Nan Brooklyn — armed groups continued violence in central Port-au-Prince, consolidating control over territories seized during the May 26 attack. Gang forces installed new leadership in the neighborhoods of Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, and Delmas 2 and 4 — an arc of central Port-au-Prince neighborhoods representing a further consolidation of the gang territorial perimeter around the government-held city center corridor. The May 26–27 Nan Brooklyn offensive extends the pattern of gang territorial expansion documented across adjacent zones throughout May 2026: the May 10 Cité Soleil/Cul-de-Sac Plain intra-Viv Ansanm clashes (30,000+ displaced); the May 25 Krache Dife attack on the Delmas 6 IDP camp (2 killed, 24 houses burned); and the ongoing closure of MSF's Cité Soleil hospital (now Day 18). The installation of new gang commanders across seized neighborhoods indicates a territorial consolidation rather than a fluid combat operation — a doctrinal shift consistent with Viv Ansanm's strategy of permanently embedding governance structures in captured areas. This pattern of incremental territorial encirclement directly contradicts PM Fils-Aimé's May 1 claim that gang control had receded from ~90% to ~75% under early GSF joint operations. The Haitian National Police, severely outnumbered and outgunned, has been unable to contest the gang advance in these zones. The GSF's ~800-person advance force remains exclusively deployed in Port-au-Prince's city center, providing no security coverage in the areas affected by the May 26–27 violence.

media.caption: PassBlue: The new UN-backed anti-gang force arrives in Haiti as violence surges — context for ongoing territorial seizures in Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, Delmas 2 and 4 during May 26-27 offensive

title: GSF Full Operations Scheduled to Launch June 1 — Force at ~800 Personnel; MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 18, No Reopening Timeline
detail: As of May 27, 2026, the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) — the UN-authorized multinational security mission that succeeded the Kenya-led MSS on April 28 — is scheduled to formally begin full operations on June 1, 2026, a milestone confirmed in Haitian media coverage. The advance force currently numbers approximately 800 personnel: 400+ Chadian troops (of a pledged 1,500 expected by June 2026), approximately 75 Guatemalans, and approximately 70 Salvadorans. The force is commanded by Mongolian Major General Erdenebat Batsuuri, who arrived Haiti on May 14. The June 1 full operations launch occurs against a backdrop of deteriorating security: on May 26–27, gang forces seized Nan Brooklyn, Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, and Delmas 2 and 4 in central Port-au-Prince — zones just outside the narrow city center corridor where the GSF currently operates. Despite pledges exceeding the authorized 5,500-person ceiling from 13 contributing nations (with over $200M pledged and $59M disbursed), the GSF will enter full operations at less than 15% of its eventual authorized strength. Full 5,500-person deployment is not expected until fall–end 2026. MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil simultaneously entered its 18th consecutive day of closure on May 27 — well past the threshold of any 'temporary' operational suspension. The hospital serves as the only emergency health facility for approximately 300,000 residents living under total gang control in Cité Soleil, a commune the GSF has not yet entered. No reopening timeline has been announced. The convergence of the GSF June 1 operational launch with the ongoing MSF closure, fresh gang territorial seizures, and the imminent US Supreme Court ruling on TPS for ~350,000 Haitian nationals defines Haiti's security and humanitarian trajectory as the summer of 2026 begins.

media.caption: Haitian Times: Haiti Gang Suppression Force (GSF) under new commander Batsuuri — full operations launch June 1, 2026 as violence surges and MSF Cité Soleil hospital enters Day 18 of closure

title: Haiti Inaugurates First Specialized Judicial Units for Mass Crimes, Sexual Violence, and Financial Accountability
detail: On May 27, 2026, Haiti formally inaugurated two specialized judicial units in Port-au-Prince — representing the first formal accountability mechanism for atrocity crimes since the crisis began in July 2021. The first unit comprises 25 magistrates handling mass crimes, sexual violence, kidnapping, and human trafficking — categories describing the bulk of documented gang violence. The second unit handles financial crimes, corruption, embezzlement, and electoral fraud. Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, attending the inauguration, declared: 'The law prevails over guns.' Human rights organizations FJKL (Fondasyon Je Klere) and CARDH (Centre d'Analyse et de Recherche en Droits de l'Homme) welcomed the development but noted a critical limitation: both units' jurisdiction is confined to Port-au-Prince's Court of First Instance, excluding crimes committed in the Artibonite, Centre, Sud-Est, and other departments where the worst atrocities have occurred. The specialized units' actual operational capacity remains severely constrained by gang control of most of Port-au-Prince, intimidation of witnesses and judges, and the near-impossibility of arresting most of the accused. None of the gang leaders responsible for the Pont-Sondé massacre (October 2024), the Wharf Jérémie massacre (December 2024), or the Jean-Denis massacre (March 2026) have been arrested. The inauguration nonetheless represents a structural step toward judicial accountability — coming on the same day that gang forces were consolidating control of Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, Delmas 2, and Delmas 4 just outside the government-held city center corridor.

media.caption: Haitian Times: Haiti inaugurates specialized judicial units for mass crimes and financial accountability — PM declares 'The law prevails over guns,' May 27, 2026
